What is HyperIso ?
ans: HyperIso, a new standalone program for the evaluation of flavour physics observables across a wide variety of Standard Model (SM) and Beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) scenarios. The code builds on the physics heritage of SuperIso, but is implemented as a new modular software package with a modern C++ core and multiple user interfaces. In addition to native implementations for established scenarios such as the SM, the general Two-Higgs-Doublet Model (THDM), and supersymmetric models, HyperIso interfaces with the MARTY framework to compute automatically BSM Wilson coefficients at leading order.

Based on this finding, we propose SWE-Pruner Pro, which prunes tool outputs directly inside the agent. Concretely, a small head turns the agent's own internal representations into a keep-or-prune label for each line, with a length-aware embedding keyed to each tool output's line count. Across two open-weight backbones and four multi-turn benchmarks, SWE-Pruner Pro saves up to 39% of prompt and completion tokens while preserving task quality, with bounded inference overhead. question: How can you check RAG other than each query analysis?
ans: To assess retrieval quality at scale without analyzing every query, we propose a unified pipeline that combines an automated golden-set evaluation with a human-in-the-loop verification framework. This approach allows us to measure overall retrieval quality using a small set of human-annotated golden questions while maintaining continuous monitoring through automated metrics. We evaluate retrieval quality across three dimensions: relevance, retrieval efficiency, and robustness. For relevance, we compute NDCG and MRR using a human-annotated golden set of questions and their corresponding ground-truth papers. This golden set is constructed by mining paper titles and abstracts and verifying them through human evaluation. To enhance dataset diversity and coverage, we augment the golden set with two supplementary corpora: MedQA for medical questions and the MS MARCO Passage corpus for general domain questions. This comprehensive set of 2,375 golden questions allows us to evaluate retrieval quality on a large and diverse dataset without incurring the high cost of manual annotation for every query. Retrieval efficiency is assessed by measuring the latency of the retriever. We record the time taken to retrieve relevant documents and compute descriptive statistics to identify any performance bottlenecks. Robustness is evaluated by analyzing the consistency of retrieval results under perturbed inputs. We apply two types of perturbations—synonym replacement and paraphrasing—to the golden questions and measure the degradation in retrieval quality. This helps us understand how sensitive the retriever is to variations in query phrasing and ensures that it performs reliably across different input styles. By integrating these automated metrics with a human-validated golden set, our unified framework provides a scalable and efficient method for monitoring and improving retrieval quality in RAG systems. This approach allows us to maintain high-quality retrieval while minimizing the need for continuous manual evaluation.
